In the building-contract appeal discussed on 2022-10-31, Grounds 6 and 7 concerned the completion date under the parties’ 2009 contract. Ground 6 challenged the Tribunal’s finding that the works were complete on 20 October 2010, when the Final Occupation Certificate (FOC) was issued; Ground 7 sought leave to appeal on the basis that the finding was against the weight of the evidence. The Tribunal had reasoned that the builder was responsible for obtaining approvals, that the FOC formed part of the contractual building works, and that the owners’ receipt of the FOC marked completion for the purposes of s 3B(1) of the HB Act.

The appellate court concluded that the Tribunal had erred in interpreting the contract. The standard-form Housing Industry Association (HIA) contract defined “building works” as physical works to be carried out, completed and handed over under the contract, including variations. “Practical completion” meant completion of those works apart from minor omissions or defects that did not prevent their reasonable use for their usual purpose. Clause 7.1 required the party named in Schedule 1, Item 11—the builder—to obtain and pay for building and planning approvals. The court held that this approval obligation did not make the FOC part of the physical building works, and that receipt of the FOC was not necessary for practical completion.
records.topic: Contract interpretation: building works and practical completion

records.text: The HIA contract’s clause 26.2(c) provided that the final progress claim was payable on practical completion and was to include an occupancy certificate if required by applicable legislation. Clause 26.7 required the owner to make final payment within five working days after practical completion and receipt of the relevant documentation. The appellate court considered these provisions but held that they did not make the FOC part of the physical building works or a necessary condition of practical completion.

The appellate court concluded that the Tribunal erred in finding that the completion date was 20 October 2010. Because of that conclusion, the court did not need to decide Ground 7, which challenged the finding as against the weight of the evidence. The court noted that its consideration of Grounds 6 and 7 was not strictly necessary in light of its findings on Grounds 2 and 3, but addressed them for completeness.

On 2022-10-31, the appellate court allowed the appeal in part, set aside the Tribunal’s orders of 16 March 2020, remitted the matter to the Tribunal for rehearing, and ordered the owners to pay the builder’s appeal costs.

On 2022-11-08, an aircraft landed on the roof of the mud-brick apartment complex where Odyl, living as Theyla Keth, resided in Erethel. Odyl put on a hooded cloak and took a walking stick to confront the person responsible, then found Val Renberg outside. Val wore plain brown leathers rather than her usual Co-Op flight suit or white-and-gold clothing; her angular face, severe hairstyle, dark-green gaze, and goggles pushed onto her forehead were unchanged. Val said Odyl’s name, took Odyl’s hands, and embraced Odyl tightly. Odyl trembled, felt her heart race, and became tearful; Odyl was barefoot and smelled Val’s sweat and leather.

Odyl and Val sat on the living-room sofa among piles of books and media. records.text: On 2022-11-08, Val Renberg took a small folded square of paper from her leather jacket and placed it on the table in front of Odyl. Odyl had slipped the letter into Val’s jacket pocket after Odyl and Val spent their last night together making love all night; Odyl had written about Odyl’s feelings and concerns and feared they might never meet again. Seeing the letter brought back memories, and Odyl struggled to contain her emotions while Val sat silently beside Odyl, waiting for Odyl to speak.

On 2023-05-15, the user asked for information about Java moss (Vesicularia dubyana), including how to care for it and its preferred lighting and water conditions.

Java moss (Vesicularia dubyana) can tolerate low to moderate aquarium lighting. The assistant advised that it can survive at 1–2 watts per gallon and grow faster and more densely at 2–4 watts per gallon; direct sunlight should be avoided because it may scorch or discolor the moss.
Java moss can grow in water temperatures of 68–82°F (20–28°C) and pH 6.0–7.5, and tolerates a wide range of water hardness, doing best in soft to moderately hard water.

The assistant advised attaching Java moss to rock, driftwood, or another decoration with a plant weight or thread; providing good water circulation; and fertilizing sparingly, such as with a balanced water-soluble fertilizer at half the recommended dose. It can also be attached to mesh to form a carpet, or used as a background or mid-water decoration. It may shelter and provide food for shrimp.

The assistant said Java moss may develop algae on its surface, particularly in high light, and suggested cleaning it with a soft-bristled brush or magnetic algae scraper. Browning or yellowing may indicate excessive light, poor water circulation, or insufficient nutrients.
